issues.legal_issue: The term family member in a residential-tenancy non-residence provision includes near blood relations who lived with the tenant and remain in the premises after the tenant leaves.
material_facts: The tenant had lived in the rented home with his mother, brother and sister.
After the tenant moved abroad, his mother and brother remained in the home, and the family members continued to reside there when the eviction application was filed.
The landlord argued that the relatives ceased to be members of the tenant’s family when the tenant moved abroad.
issues.conclusion: Family is to be construed broadly to include near relations living with the head of the family; the tenant’s departure did not make the relatives cease to be members of his family.
issues.legal_principle: In applying section 14(1)(d) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, family is not restricted to a narrow household unit and includes near relations who actually live with the head of the family. The court relied on the beneficial object of the Act, the inclusion of parents and persons ordinarily living with a tenant in section 2(1)(i)(iii), as amended by Act 18 of 1976, and Price v. Gould, G.V. Shukla v. Shri Prabhu Ram Sukhram Dass Ojha, Govind Dass v. Kuldip Singh, and Hira Lal v. Banarsi Dass.

predicates.nonresidence_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking recovery of a residence on the ground that the tenant and the tenant’s family had ceased to reside there.
predicates.near_relatives_lived_with_tenant: Near blood relations lived in the premises with the tenant as members of the household.
predicates.near_relatives_remained_after_tenant_lef: Those near blood relations continued living in the premises after the tenant left.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks recovery because of non-residence, near blood relations who lived with the tenant and remain after the tenant leaves continue to count as family members.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord cannot recover a residential tenancy on the ground of non-residence when a member of the tenant’s family continues to reside in the premises during the relevant period.
material_facts: The premises had been let for residential use.
The tenant moved abroad and did not return, but his mother, brother and sister continued to reside in the premises, including throughout the six months before the eviction application.
The relatives had lived in the premises with the tenant, and the Rent Controller found that they continued residing there when the eviction action was brought.
issues.conclusion: The landlord failed to establish the requirements for eviction on the non-residence ground. The appeal was allowed, the eviction order was set aside, and the eviction action was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1)(d) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 requires proof that the premises were let for residential use, that the tenant ceased to reside there, and that no member of the tenant’s family resided there for six months immediately before the application. The provision focuses on whether the family actually resides in the premises, not solely on the tenant’s physical presence; it permits recovery only when the premises have been completely vacated by the tenant and family. The court also relied on the broad construction of family, supported by section 2(1)(i)(iii), as amended by Act 18 of 1976, and Price v. Gould, G.V. Shukla v. Shri Prabhu Ram Sukhram Dass Ojha, Govind Dass v. Kuldip Singh, and Hira Lal v. Banarsi Dass.

rule.if: nonresidence_eviction_proceeding and residential_premises and tenant_ceased_to_reside and family_member_resided_throughout_relevant_period

predicates.nonresidence_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking recovery of a residence on the ground that the tenant and the tenant’s family had ceased to reside there.
predicates.residential_premises: The premises were let for use as a residence.
predicates.tenant_ceased_to_reside: The tenant stopped residing in the premises.
predicates.family_member_resided_throughout_relevan: At least one member of the tenant’s family continued to reside in the premises throughout the period immediately preceding the eviction application.

issues.definition: A landlord cannot obtain eviction for non-residence when the premises were let as a residence, the tenant stopped living there, but a family member continued to live there throughout the relevant period.
